items.explanation: A scalar subquery returns one row and one column.
items.example: SELECT product_name, unit_price FROM products WHERE unit_price > (SELECT AVG(unit_price) FROM products) ORDER BY unit_price DESC;

items.operation: Match a list from a query
items.explanation: Semi-join: keeps rows whose value appears in the subquery.
items.example: SELECT company_name FROM customers WHERE customer_id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM orders WHERE freight > 150);
items.expected: Customers with at least one order over 150 freight.

items.explanation: Stops at the first match; the select list is irrelevant.
items.example: SELECT s.company_name FROM suppliers s WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM products p WHERE p.supplier_id = s.supplier_id AND p.unit_price > 50);
items.expected: Suppliers of at least one product over 50.

items.explanation: NULL-safe anti-join; prefer it to NOT IN.
items.example: SELECT customer_id FROM customers c WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE o.customer_id = c.customer_id);

items.syntax: WHERE col > (SELECT AVG(col) FROM t2 WHERE t2.g = t1.g)
items.explanation: The inner query refers to the outer row and runs per row (logically).
items.example: SELECT p.product_name, p.category_id, p.unit_price FROM products p WHERE p.unit_price > (SELECT AVG(p2.unit_price) FROM products p2 WHERE p2.category_id = p.category_id) ORDER BY p.category_id;
items.expected: Products priced above their category average.

items.explanation: A derived table needs an alias; use it to filter on aggregates or window results.
items.example: SELECT * FROM (SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS n FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id) t WHERE n > 2 ORDER BY n DESC;

items.syntax: SELECT a, (SELECT … WHERE b.k = a.k) FROM a
items.explanation: Correlated scalar subquery as a column; returns NULL when nothing matches.
items.example: SELECT c.customer_id, (SELECT MAX(o.order_date) FROM orders o WHERE o.customer_id = c.customer_id) AS last_order FROM customers c LIMIT 5;
items.expected: 5 customers with their last order date.

items.explanation: ALL: true for every value; ANY: true for at least one.
items.example: SELECT product_name, unit_price FROM products WHERE unit_price > ALL (SELECT unit_price FROM products WHERE category_id = 2);
items.expected: Products more expensive than every category-2 product.
